MRK.rationale: MRK's Q1 2026 results reveal a severe earnings collapse: net income swung to -$4.24B (EPS -$1.72) from +$5.08B (EPS +$2.01) YoY, driven by a $9B one-time Cidara acquisition charge that inflated R&D expenses to $12.59B (+247.8% YoY). While revenue grew 4.9% YoY to $16.29B and beat estimates, the operating margin collapsed to -21.7% from 37.8% a year ago. The balance sheet deteriorated with total equity declining from $51.91B (Sep 2025) to $45.93B (Mar 2026) and total liabilities rising to $82.75B. Valuation is extremely stretched: P/E of 33.17x is at the top of its 365-day range (11.1-33.9x), representing a 3x expansion from the ~11x level a year ago, while ROE has collapsed from 36.1% to 19.5% and net margin from 27.3% to 13.6%. The stock has rallied 41% from its Aug 2025 low of $84.99 to $119.89, yet fundamentals have materially worsened. The Keytruda patent cliff (late 2028) remains the dominant structural risk, with the drug accounting for ~49% of FY2025 sales, and the company's strategy to convert patients to Qlex faces significant execution risk. Gardasil sales declined 39% in FY2025, increasing pipeline dependency. Near-term catalysts are limited: the ASCO meeting (May 21) has already passed, and the next earnings report is not until August. The $5.7B Terns Pharmaceuticals acquisition adds further balance sheet pressure. Macro headwinds include rising 10Y Treasury yields (4.45%) and elevated oil prices ($92.65/bbl) that could pressure healthcare spending. News sentiment is mixed (mean 0.613 over 90 days) with no clear positive inflection. All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating fundamentals, extreme valuation vs. history, and no credible near-term re-rating catalyst.
